ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of rhombus ABCD is 6, and $\angle D = 120^\circ$. Point E is the midpoint of AB, and point P is a moving point on diagonal AC. What is the minimum value of $BP+EP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $DP$, $BD$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rhombus, \\
thus point $B$ and point $D$ are symmetric with respect to $AC$, \\
thus $DP=PB$, \\
thus $PB+PE=DP+PE \geq DE$, \\
when $DE \perp AB$, the value of $PB+PE$ is minimal, \\
since $\angle D=120^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DAB=60^\circ$, \\
since $AD=AB$, \\
thus $\triangle ABD$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
since $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$, \\
thus $DE \perp AB$, \\
since $AB=6$, \\
thus $DE=3\sqrt{3}$, \\
thus the minimum value of $PB+PE$ is $\boxed{3\sqrt{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an obliquely placed rhombus ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; diagonal AC connects from A to C, and point P is marked on diagonal AC; point E is on side AB, and the figure also draws the line segment from D to E and the line segments from E and B to P. The problem gives that the side length of the rhombus is 6, ∠D=120°, E is the midpoint of AB, and P moves on AC. Reasoning: Because P is restricted to diagonal AC, and the rhombus is symmetric about diagonal AC, taking vertex B and D to be symmetric, for any such P, BP=DP. Therefore BP+EP=DP+EP. By the triangle inequality, DP+EP≥DE; equality is attained when P is located at the intersection point of segment DE and AC, and D, P, E are collinear, so the minimum value is DE. Next calculate DE. Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so ∠DAB=180°−120°=60°. Also AB=AD=6, therefore △ABD is an equilateral triangle with side length 6. E is the midpoint of AB, so AE=3, and DE is the height of the equilateral triangle: DE=√(6²−3²)=√27=3√3. The intersection point of this DE and AC is indeed on AC inside the figure, so equality can be attained. Final answer: The minimum value of BP+EP is 3√3.
